semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {الجوار}: the majority read it with kasra on the rāʾ, because it is a manqūṣ noun (one ending in a defective yāʾ) on the pattern mafāʿil, and the yāʾ is dropped in pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. ʿAbd Allāh and al-Ḥasan read — and it is also transmitted from Abū ʿAmr — «الجَوارُ» with ḍamma on the rāʾ, as if the omitted letter were forgotten; from this is:
4173 - لها ثنايا أربعٌ حِسانُ ... وأربعٌ فثَغْرُها ثَمانُ (She has four fine front teeth, and four more, so her mouth [has] eight.) This is like their saying «هذا شاكٌ». The explanation of this has already been given in al-Aʿrāf at His saying: {وَمِن فَوْقِهِمْ غَوَاشٍ} [al-Aʿrāf: 41].
His saying: {المنشئات}: Ḥamza and Abū Bakr — with a disagreement in what is transmitted from him — read it with kasra on the shīn, meaning that they produce the waves by their running, or produce the voyage, coming and going, or [they are] those that have raised their shuruʿ, i.e. their sails. The shirāʿ is the sail (al-qilʿ). From Mujāhid: whenever it raises its sail it is among the munshiʾāt, otherwise it is not among them. Attributing the raising to them is figurative (majāz), as one says: «أنْشَأتِ السحابةُ المطرَ» (the cloud produced the rain). The rest read it with fatḥa, and it is a passive participle (ism mafʿūl), i.e. Allah or people produced them, or raised their sails. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «المُنَشَّآت» with a doubled shīn, for intensiveness. Al-Ḥasan read «المُنْشات» in the singular, with the hamza changed into an alif and with a drawn-out tāʾ (tāʾ majdhūba) in the writing; he made the adjective singular, relying on the noun described to convey the plurality, as in His saying: {أَزْوَاجٌ مُّطَهَّرَةٌ} [al-Baqara: 25]. As for his changing the hamza into an alif, although its regular treatment would be bayna bayna (a sound between hamza and the long vowel), that is an exaggeration in lightening, as in his saying:
4174 - إنَّ السِّباعَ لَتَهْدَا في مَرابِضِها ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (The beasts of prey are indeed at rest in their lairs …)
i.e. «لتهدَأ». As for writing it with the drawn-out tāʾ, that follows its pronunciation in continuous speech (waṣl). And «في البحر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «المُنْشِئات» or «المنشَآت». Its being written with a yāʾ after the shīn in the codices of Iraq strengthens the reading with kasra, and its being written without it strengthens the reading with fatḥa; they omitted the alif as it is omitted in all sound feminine plurals. And «كالأَعْلام» is a ḥāl (circumstantial): either from the latent (mustatir) pronoun concealed in «المُنْشَآت», or from «الجوار»; both amount to the same meaning. Al-aʿlām are mountains, the plural of ʿalam. He said:
4175 - رُبَّما أَوْفَيْتُ في عَلَم ... تَرْفَعَنْ ثوبي شَمالاتُ (Many a time I have climbed up on a mountain-top, north winds lifting my garment.)

semin-durr:26-26.t: And His saying: {كُلُّ مَنْ عَلَيْهَا فَانٍ}: He gave precedence to those endowed with reason over others, while all of them are meant. The pronoun in «عليها» refers to the earth. Some of them said: "even though it has not been mentioned, as in His saying: {حتى تَوَارَتْ بالحجاب} [Ṣād: 32]." This speaker has been refuted, and they said: rather, it was mentioned before, in His saying: {والأرض وَضَعَهَا} [al-Raḥmān: 10].

semin-durr:27-27.t: His saying: {ذُو الجلال}: the majority read «ذو» with wāw, as an adjective (naʿt) of «الوجه». Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read «ذي» with yāʾ, as an adjective of «ربِّك». There will come a disagreement among the Seven [readers] at the end of the sūra, if Allah the Exalted wills.

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {يَسْأَلُهُ مَن فِي السماوات}: there are two views on it. The first: it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «وَجْه», and what governs it is «يَبْقَى», i.e. it remains being asked by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.
His saying: {كُلَّ يَوْمٍ}: accusative (manṣūb) by the [verbal notion of] settledness (istiqrār) contained in the khabar (predicate), which is His saying «في شَأْنٍ». Al-shaʾn: the affair.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {سَنَفْرُغُ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «سَيَفْرُغُ» with yāʾ, i.e. Allah the Exalted will attend. The rest of the Seven read it with the nūn of majesty. The rāʾ has ḍamma in both readings, and this is the most eloquent dialect, the dialect of the Ḥijāz. Al-Aʿraj read it with fatḥa on the rāʾ together with the nūn, and it admits two explanations. The first: that it is from «فَرَغَ» with fatḥa on the rāʾ in the past tense, and it was given fatḥa in the imperfect because of the guttural letter. The second: that «فَرِغَ» with kasra on the ʿayn [of the root] has been heard, so this would be its imperfect; this is the dialect of Tamīm. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and Abū al-Sammāl read «سَنِفْرَغُ» with kasra on the imperfect prefix and fatḥa on the rāʾ; its justification is clear from what was said earlier in al-Fātiḥa. Abū Ḥātim said: "It is the dialect of lower Muḍar." Al-Aʿmash, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibrāhīm read «سَنِفْرَغُ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ [with two dots] below, as a passive. [Translator's note: the text as printed writes «سَنِفْرَغُ» here, while describing a reading with a ḍamma on a yāʾ, i.e. «سَيُفْرَغُ»; translated as written.] ʿĪsā also read with fatḥa on the nūn of majesty and kasra on the rāʾ. Al-Aʿraj also read with fatḥa on the yāʾ and on the rāʾ, and it is transmitted from Abū ʿAmr. The reading of «أيها» has already been discussed in al-Nūr. "Attending" (al-farāgh) here is a metaphor (istiʿāra). It has also been said: it means "directing oneself towards (al-qaṣd)". A verse of Jarīr was cited:
4176 - ألانَ وقد فَرَغْتُ إلى نُمَيْرٍ ... فهذا حينَ كُنْتُ لهمُ عَذاباً (Now that I have turned to [deal with] Numayr, this is the time I have become a torment to them.) And al-Zajjāj cited:
4177 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فَرَغْتُ إلى العبدِ المقيَّدِ في الحِجْلِ (… I turned to the slave fettered in the shackle.)
This is supported by the reading of Ubayy «سَنَفْرُغُ إليكم», i.e. "We shall direct Ourselves to you." Al-thaqalān are the jinn and mankind, because they are the two weighty burdens (thaqal) of the earth. It has also been said: because of their being weighed down by sins. It has also been said: al-thaqal is mankind, for their nobility, and the jinn were called thus figuratively, by contiguity. Al-thaqal is something great and noble. In the hadith: «إني تاركٌ فيكم ثَقَلَيْن كتابَ الله وعِتْرتي» ("I am leaving among you two weighty things: the Book of Allah and my family").

semin-durr:33-33.t: His saying: {فانفذوا}: an imperative expressing incapacity (amr taʿjīz). Al-nufūdh is going out quickly. It has been mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara that what has nūn as its first radical and fāʾ as its second indicates going out, like «نَفَق» and «نَفَرَ». And «إلاَّ بسُلْطان» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), or attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إنْ اسْتَطَعْتما» as addressed to the two thaqal [jinn and mankind]; by right he should have kept to one course and read «أنْ تَنْفَذا، لا تنفُذان». The majority treated it like His saying: {وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ المؤمنين اقتتلوا} [al-Ḥujurāt: 9], since under each of the two there are many individuals. The wording of the dual is observed in His saying afterwards: «يُرْسَلُ عليكما», so Zayd's reading is not far-fetched.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {شُوَاظٌ}: Ibn Kathīr read it with kasra on the shīn, and the rest with ḍamma; they are two dialectal forms with one meaning. Al-shuwāẓ: it has been said: a flame with smoke. It has also been said: rather, it is pure flame. It has also been said: the red flame. It has also been said: it is the smoke coming out of the flame. Ruʾba said:
4178 - ونارَ حَرْبٍ تُسْعِرُ الشُّواظا ... (And a fire of war kindling the flames.) And Ḥassān said:
4179 - هَجَوتُكَ فاخْتَضَعْتَ لها بذُلٍّ ... بقافِيَة تَأَجَّجُ كالشُّواظِ (I lampooned you, and you bowed to it in humiliation, with a rhyme blazing like flames.)
And «يُرْسَلُ» is passive; this is the reading of the majority. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «نُرْسِلُ» with nūn, and «شواظاً ونُحاساً» in the accusative. And «مِنْ نار» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «شواظ», or attached to «يُرْسَلُ».
His saying: «ونُحاس»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it in the genitive, conjoined to «نارٍ», and the rest in the nominative, conjoined to «شُواظ». Al-nuḥās: it has been said it is the well-known brass, which Allah the Exalted melts and torments them with. It has also been said: smoke that has no flame with it. Al-Khalīl said: it is well known in the speech of the Arabs, and he cited for al-Aʿshā:
4180 - يُضيْءُ كضَوْءِ سراجِ السَّلِيْ ... طِ لم يَجْعَلِ اللَّهُ فيه نُحاسا (It shines like the light of an oil lamp in which Allah has put no smoke.)
Its nūn may take ḍamma or kasra; Mujāhid, Ṭalḥa and al-Kalbī read it with kasra. Ibn Jundub read «ونَحْسٌ», as in His saying: {فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ} [al-Qamar: 19]. Ibn Abī Bakra and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «ونَحُسُّ» with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the sīn doubled, from His saying: {إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ} [Āl ʿImrān: 152], i.e. "and We kill with the punishment". Ibn Abī Isḥāq also read «ونَحَُِسٍ» with ḍamma, fatḥa and kasra on the ḥāʾ, and the sīn in the genitive. And al-Ḥasan and al-Qāḍī [read]
«ونُحُسٍ» with two ḍammas and the sīn in the genitive. Zayd's reading «ونُحاساً» in the accusative has already been mentioned, being conjoined to «شواظاً» in his reading.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {فَإِذَا انشقت}: its apodosis (jawāb) is implied (muqaddar), i.e. "you would see a great terror", or "what happened would happen".
His saying: {وَرْدَةً}, i.e. like a rose. It has been said: it is the well-known flower that is smelled; He likened it to it in redness. And [a verse] was cited:
4181 - فلو كُنْتُ وَرْداً لَوْنُه لعَشِقْنَني ... ولكنَّ ربي شانَني بسَواديا (Had I been rose-coloured, they would have loved me; but my Lord marred me with my blackness.)
It has also been said: it is from the colour of the bay horse (al-faras al-ward), and it was made feminine because the sky is feminine. Al-Farrāʾ said: "He meant the colour of the bay horse, which in spring tends to yellow, in winter to red, and in the severity of the cold to dust-colour; so He likened the changing colours of the sky to the changing colours of the bay among horses." ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «وَرْدَةٌ» in the nominative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "In the sense: 'and there came to be a rose sky'; it is of the kind of speech called tajrīd (abstraction), as in his saying:
4182 - فَلَئِنْ بَقِيْتُ لأَرْحَلَنَّ بِغَزْوةٍ ... تَحْوِي الغنائمَ أو يموتَُ كريمُ (If I remain alive, I shall set out on a raid that gathers spoils, or a noble man dies.)" His saying: {كالدهان}: it may be a second khabar (predicate), or an adjective (naʿt) of «وردة», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the noun (ism) of «كانت». Concerning «الدِّهان» there are two views. The first: it is the plural of «دُهْن», like «قُرْط» and «قِراط», and «رُمْح» and «رِماح»; and it is in the sense of His saying: {يَوْمَ تَكُونُ السمآء كالمهل} [al-Maʿārij: 8].
That is the dregs of oil. The second: it is a singular noun. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "the name of what one anoints with, like «الجِزام» and «الإِدام»", and he cited:
4183 - كأنَّهما مَزادَتا مُتَعَجِّلٍ ... فَرِيَّانِ لَمَّا تُدْهَنا بدِهان (As if they were the two water-skins of a hasty man, new, not yet treated with oil.)
Someone else said: it is red leather, and he cited for al-Aʿshā:
4184 - وأَجْرَدَ مِنْ كِرامِ الخَيْلِ طِرْفٍ ... كأنَّ على شَواكِله دِهانا (And a short-haired, noble steed of the best horses, as if there were red leather on its flanks.)
i.e. red leather. This may possibly be a plural. It is supported by what Mundhir ibn Saʿīd cited: 4185 - يَبِعْنَ الدِّهانَ الحُمْرَ كلَّ عَشِيَّةٍ ... بموسِمِ بَدْرٍ أو بسُوْقِ عُكاظِ (They sell the red hides every evening at the season of Badr or in the market of ʿUkāẓ.)
His saying «الحُمْرَ» supports its being a plural; though it may be said that it is like their saying: «أهلك الناسَ الدينارُ الحُمْرُ والدرهمُ البِيْضُ» (the red dinar and the white dirham have ruined people), except that this goes against the basic rule. It has also been said: it was likened to oil (al-dihān), i.e. olive oil, for its melting and swirling; and it has also been said: for its gleam.

semin-durr:39-39.t: His saying: {فَيَوْمَئِذٍ}: the tanwīn is a substitute for the clause, i.e. "on the day when the sky is split". The fāʾ in «فيومئذٍ» is [the fāʾ of] the apodosis of the condition (jawāb al-sharṭ). It has also been said: [the apodosis] is omitted, i.e. "when the sky is split, you will see a terrifying matter", and the like. The hāʾ in «ذَنْبه» [refers to one of the two mentioned], and the pronoun of the other is implied, i.e. "nor will a jinn be asked about his sin" either. What puts the adverb in the accusative is «لا يُسأَلُ», and «لا» does not prevent [this]. The disagreement of people about it has already been given in al-Fātiḥa. The reading «جأَنّ» with hamza has also been given there.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
Ḥammād ibn Abī Sulaymān read «بسِيْمائِهم» with the long vowel (madd). The discussion of this has already been given at the end of al-Baqara.
His saying: {فَيُؤْخَذُ بالنواصي}: «يُؤْخَذُ» is transitive, yet it is made transitive with the bāʾ, because it has been made to include the meaning of «يُسْحَبُ» (is dragged); al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said this. But «سحب» is only made transitive with «على»; the Exalted said: {يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النار على وُجُوهِهِمْ} [al-Qamar: 48]. So he ought to have said: it has been made to include the meaning of «يُدَعُّوْن», i.e. "they are shoved". Makkī said: "One only says «أَخَذْتُ الناصِيةَ» and «أخَذْتُ بالناصية». If you said «أَخَذْتُ الدابَّةَ بالناصيةِ», it would not be permissible. It is reported from the Arabs: «أَخَذْتُ الخِطامَ» and «أَخَذْتُ بالخِطام» with the same meaning. It has been said that its implied form is: 'so each one will be seized by the forelocks'; this is not correct, because it is not made transitive to two objects, one of them with the bāʾ, for the reason we mentioned. It may be made transitive to two objects, one of them with a preposition other than the bāʾ, as in «أَخَذْتُ ثوباً من زيد» (I took a garment from Zayd).
This meaning is other than the first, so another object does not sit well with the bāʾ, unless you make it mean 'because of', in which case you may say «أَخَذْتُ زيداً بعمروٍ», i.e. because of him and for his offence." End of quotation. What he said is open to objection (fīhi naẓar), because you say «أَخَذْتُ الثوبَ بدرهمٍ» (I took the garment for a dirham), so it has been made transitive with something other than «مِنْ» as well, in a meaning other than the one he mentioned.
The al- in «النواصي» and «الأقدام» is not a substitute for a pronoun according to the Basrans, so the implied form is "by the forelocks [belonging] to them"; according to the Kufans it is a substitute [for the pronoun]. Al-nāṣiya is the front of the head; this has been treated fully in Hūd. In the hadith of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: «ما لكم لا تَنْصُون مَيِّتكم» ("Why do you not comb out your dead person?"), i.e. you do not stretch out his forelock. Al-naṣiyy is a good pasture. Their saying «فلانٌ ناصيةُ القوم» (so-and-so is the forelock of the people) may be from this, meaning that he is good and beneficial, or like their saying: "he is the head of the people".

semin-durr:43-43.t: His saying: {هذه جَهَنَّمُ}: i.e. it will be said to them. And «آن» means hot, at the extreme of heat. It is a manqūṣ noun like «قاضٍ»: one says «أنى يَأْني فهو آن», like «قَضى يَقْضي فهو قاضٍ». It has already been discussed in al-Aḥzāb. The majority read «يَطوفون», from «طاف». ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān read «يُطافُون» as a passive, from «أطافهم غيرُهم» (others made them go round). Al-Aʿmash, Ṭalḥa and Ibn Miqsam read «يُطَوِّفُون» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, fatḥa on the ṭāʾ and kasra on the doubled wāw, i.e. they make themselves go round. A group read «يَطَّوَّون» with the ṭāʾ and the wāw doubled; the original form is «يتطَوَّفون». [Translator's note: the printed text has «يَطَّوَّون»; the stated original «يتطَوَّفون» implies «يَطَّوَّفون». Translated as written.]

semin-durr:46-46.t:
His saying: {مَقَامَ رَبِّهِ}: it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or it may be [a noun of] place. If it is a maṣdar, it may be annexed to its agent, i.e. his Lord's standing over him and His keeping record of his deeds, from His saying: {أَفَمَنْ هُوَ قَآئِمٌ على كُلِّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ} [al-Raʿd: 33] — this meaning is reported from Mujāhid; or it may be annexed to its object, the meaning being: standing up for the rights of Allah so that he does not neglect them. If it is [a noun of] place, the annexation is by the slightest connection, since people stand before Allah the Exalted for the reckoning in the open plains of the Resurrection; it has been said: in it is the station of Allah. The apparent meaning is that the two gardens are for one person who fears. It has also been said: one garden for the one who fears among mankind, and another for the one who fears among the jinn, so it is of the type of distribution (tawzīʿ). It has also been said that «مَقام» here is intrusive (muqḥam), the implied form being "and for him who fears his Lord", and [a verse] was cited:
4186 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ونَفَيْتُ عنه ... مَقامَ الذِّئْبِ كالرَّجُلِ اللعينِ (… and I drove away from it the wolf['s station], like the accursed man.)
i.e. I drove away the wolf. This is not good, because the addition of a noun is not an easy matter.

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {ذَوَاتَآ}: an adjective (ṣifa) of «جَنَّتان», or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "they are possessors of". In the dual of «ذات» there are two usages: returning to the original form, for its original form is «ذَوْيَة», the second radical being wāw and the third yāʾ, since it is the feminine of «ذو»; and the second: forming the dual on the surface form, so one says «ذاتا».
Al-afnān: there are two views on it. The first: it is the plural of «فَنَن», like «طَلَل», which is the branch. Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī said:
4187 - بكاءَ حمامةٍ تَدْعو هَدِيلاً ... مُفَجَّعةٍ على فَنَنٍ تُغَنِّي (Like the weeping of a bereaved dove calling for its mate, singing on a branch.)
Another said:
4188 - رُبَّ وَرْقاءَ هَتُوفٍ بالضُّحى ... ذاتِ شَجْوٍ صَدَحَتْ في فَنَنِ (Many a grey, cooing dove in the forenoon, full of grief, has sung out on a branch.) Another said:
4189 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... على كلِّ أفنانِ العِضاهِ تَرُوْقُ (… pleasing on every branch of the thorn-trees.)
The second: it is the plural of «فَنّ», like «دَنّ», and Ibn ʿAbbās pointed to this. The meaning is: possessing kinds and varieties. They cited:
4190 - ومِنْ كلِّ أفنانِ اللَّذاذَةِ والصِّبا ... لَهَوْتُ به والعيشُ أخضرُ ناضِرُ (In every kind of pleasure and youthful play I have amused myself, while life was green and fresh.)
Except that the usual plural of «فَنّ» is «فُنون».

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {مُتَّكِئِينَ}: it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَنْ» in His saying «ولِمَنْ خافَ»; it was only put in the plural following the meaning of «مَنْ», after the singular following its wording. It has also been said: a ḥāl whose governor is omitted, i.e. "they enjoy themselves, reclining". It has also been said: accusative by specification (ikhtiṣāṣ). The majority read «فُرُش» with two ḍammas, and Abū Ḥaywa with a ḍamma and a sukūn, which is a lightened form of it.
His saying: {بَطَآئِنُهَا مِنْ إِسْتَبْرَقٍ}: this clause may be resumptive; the apparent view is that it is an adjective (ṣifa) of «فُرُش». As for «مِنْ إستبرق», the discussion of «الاستبرق» and what has been said about it has already been given in Sūrat al-Kahf. Abū al-Baqāʾ said here: "The original of the word is a verb on the pattern «اسْتَفْعَلَ»; when it was used as a name, its hamza was made a hamzat qaṭʿ (disjunctive hamza). It has also been said: it is foreign. It has been read with the hamza dropped and kasra on the nūn, and this is a mistake, because that does not occur in nouns, but only in verbal nouns and verbs." End of quotation. As for his saying "and this is a mistake, because that does not occur" to the end — he means that dropping the hamza in continuous speech occurs only in verbs and verbal nouns, whereas in nouns their hamzas are not dropped because they are disjunctive hamzas. This statement is more deserving of being called a mistake: firstly, we do not concede that this reading is a case of dropping the disjunctive hamza by treating it like the connective hamza (hamzat al-waṣl); rather, it is a case of transferring the vowel of the hamza to the quiescent letter before it. The vowel of the hamza was a kasra, so the vowel of the nūn is a transferred vowel, not a vowel for the meeting of two quiescent letters. Then his saying "only in verbs and verbal nouns" — this restriction is not correct, by agreement, since that occurs in ten nouns which are not verbal nouns; I mentioned them at the beginning of this work.
His saying: {وَجَنَى الجنتين دَانٍ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The original of «دانٍ» is «دانِوٌ», like «غازٍ», and it underwent the same weakening as it. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «وجَنِيَ» with kasra on the nūn. Its justification: he inclined (imāla) the fatḥa because of the alif, then dropped the alif because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and kept the inclination of the nūn, so it was thought to be a kasra. It has also been read «وجِنَى» with kasra on the jīm, and it is a dialectal form. Al-janā is the fruit that is picked; it is [on the pattern] faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl (passive participle), like «القَبَض» and «النَقَص».

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {فِيهِنَّ قَاصِرَاتُ}: there is disagreement about this pronoun. It has been said: it refers to the gardens. Then it may be asked: how can a dual precede and then a plural pronoun be brought?
The answer: either [one says] that the minimum plural is two, according to one view, and it has supporting evidence, most of which has been given before; or one says: it refers to the gardens indicated by «الجنتين»; or one says: every single individual has two gardens, so it is correct that they are many gardens; or that the garden contains sitting places, palaces and dwellings, so each one of them was called a garden. It has also been said: it refers to the couches (al-furush). This is a good view with little strain.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«فيهِنَّ»: in these enumerated blessings: the two gardens, the two springs, the fruit, the couches and the fruit within reach." Al-Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "There is far-fetchedness in it", and he had approved the view before it. This is open to objection (fīhi naẓar), because the usage is to say "on the couch is such-and-such", and one does not say "in the couch is such-and-such" except with strain; for this reason al-Zamakhsharī combined other things with the couches so that it would be correct for him to say «فيهن» with the preposition of containment; and because the reality is that a person is on the couches, since he is above them, whereas his being in them can only be said figuratively. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Every place in Paradise is a garden, so it is correct to say «فيهِنَّ»." Al-qāṣirāt are those who restrain their glance, i.e. their eyes, from anyone other than their husbands. Its meaning: they confine their glances to their husbands. Imruʾ al-Qays said: 4191 - مِن القاصِراتِ الطَّرْفِ لو دَبَّ مُحْوِلٌ ... من الذَّرِّ فوق الإِتْبِ منها لأَثَّرا (Of those who restrain their glance; were a year-old young ant to creep over her shift, it would leave a mark.)
«وقاصراتُ الطرفِ» is a case of annexing the active participle to its accusative [object] for lightness, since one says «قَصَرَ طَرْفَه على كذا». What the restraining is attached to is omitted because it is known, i.e. "to their husbands", as explained before. It has also been said: the meaning is that they restrain others' glance to themselves, i.e. when someone sees them, his glance does not pass on to anyone else.
His saying: {لَمْ يَطْمِثْهُنَّ}: this clause may be an adjective (naʿt) of «قاصِرات», because its annexation is a verbal (lafẓī, non-defining) annexation, as in His saying: {هذا عَارِضٌ مُّمْطِرُنَا} [al-Aḥqāf: 24] and [his saying]:
4192 - يا رُبَّ غابطِنا لو كان يَطْلُبُكمْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . (Many a one who envies us, had he sought you …)
Or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the indefinite noun is specified by the annexation. There is disagreement about this word and the one after it as transmitted from al-Kisāʾī: it is reported from him that he let the reader choose to give ḍamma to whichever of the two he wished; al-Dūrī reported from him ḍamma in the first only, and Abū al-Ḥārith reported from him ḍamma in the second only. They are two dialectal forms: one says «طَمَثَها يَطْمِثُها ويَطْمُثُها» when he has intercourse with her. The origin of al-ṭamth is intercourse leading to the flow of a virgin's blood; then every intercourse came to be called ṭamth, even if there is no blood with it. It has also been said: al-ṭamth is menstrual blood or the blood of intercourse. It has also been said: al-ṭamth is a particular touching. Al-Jaḥdarī read «يَطْمَثْهُنَّ» with fatḥa on the mīm in both words, and it is anomalous (shādhdh), since neither its second nor its third radical is a guttural letter. The pronoun in «قبلَهُمْ» refers to the husbands, indicated by His saying «قاصراتُ الطَّرْفِ», or indicated by «مُتَّكئين».

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {كَأَنَّهُنَّ الياقوت}: this clause may be an adjective (naʿt) of «قاصِرات», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it; Makkī mentioned nothing else. What al-marjān is has already been given. Al-yāqūt is a precious gem; it is said that fire does not affect it, and for that reason al-Ḥarīrī said:
4193 - وطالما أُصْلِيَ اليقاوتُ جَمْرَ غَضَا ... ثم انْطفا الجمرُ والياقوتُ ياقوتُ (How often has the ruby been exposed to the embers of ghaḍā wood; then the embers die out and the ruby is still ruby.)
i.e. it remains as it was, unaffected by it. The point of the simile, as al-Ḥasan said, is the clarity of the ruby and the whiteness of the marjān; this is on the view that it is white, which has been given before. It has also been said: the point lies in … and their preciousness; for that reason they named [women] Marjāna, Durra and the like. [Translator's note: there is a gap («. . .») in the source text here.]

semin-durr:60-60.t: Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «إلاَّ الحِسانُ», i.e. "except the beautiful houris".

semin-durr:62-62.t: His saying: {وَمِن دُونِهِمَا}: i.e. below those two previously mentioned gardens are two gardens, in rank and beauty of appearance. This is according to the apparent view that the first two are superior to the other two. The opposite has also been said, and al-Zamakhsharī preferred it.

semin-durr:66-66.t: Al-naḍkh is more than al-naḍḥ with ḥāʾ, because al-naḍḥ with ḥāʾ is sprinkling and seeping, while al-naḍkh with khāʾ is the gushing of water. Al-idhīmām is blackness and intense greenness; they were made «مُدْهامَّتيْن» (dark green) because of how well-watered they are, and this is observable to the eye; for that reason they said "the blackness of Iraq" (sawād al-ʿIrāq) because of its many trees and crops.

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying: {وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ}: some have used it as evidence that these two are not among fruit, since conjunction requires difference; so if someone swore "he will not eat fruit", he would not break his oath by eating them. Others say: it is a case of mentioning the specific after the general, by way of detailing it, as in His saying {وملائكته} [al-Baqara: 98] then saying «وجبريلَ وميكَال». This is a loose usage, because «فاكهة» is not general (ʿāmm), since it is an indefinite noun in an affirmative context; it is only unrestricted (muṭlaq). But since it applies truly to palms and pomegranates, this was said about it. [Translator's note: the source cites the verse as al-Baqara: 97; «وملائكته … وجبريل وميكال» is al-Baqara: 98.]

semin-durr:70-70.t:
His saying: {خَيْرَاتٌ}: there are two views on it. The first: it is the plural of «خَيْرَة» on the pattern faʿla with a sukūn on the second radical; one says: «امرأةٌ خَيْرَةٌ» (a good woman) and another «شَرَّةٌ» (a bad one). The second: it is the plural of «خَيْرة», lightened from «خَيِّرة»; this is indicated by the reading of Ibn Miqsam, al-Yazīdī and Bakr ibn Ḥabīb «خَيِّرات» with a doubled yāʾ. Abū ʿAmr read «خَيَرات» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, plural of «خَيْرَة»; it is anomalous (shādhdh), because the second radical is weak, except that the Banū Hudhayl treat it like a sound letter and say «جَوَزات» and «بَيَضات», and [a verse] was cited:
4194 - أخو بَيَضاتٍ رائِحٌ مُتَأَوِّبُ ... رفيقٌ بمَسْحِ المَنْكِبَيْنِ سَبُوْحُ (The keeper of eggs [an ostrich], going out in the evening and returning by night, gentle in the motion of its shoulders, a swift runner.)

semin-durr:72-72.t:
And «مَقْصورات», i.e. kept secluded. From it is «القَصْر» (the palace), because it keeps in whoever is in it; and from it is the grammarians' term «المقصور», because it is withheld from the long vowel (madd), or withheld from case-inflection (iʿrāb), or the inflection is withheld in it. Women are praised for keeping to their houses, as [Abū] Qays ibn al-Aslat said:
4195 - وتَكْسَلُ عن جيرانِها فيَزُرْنَها ... وتَعْتَلُّ عن إتْيانِهِنَّ فتُعْذَرُ (She is too languid to visit her neighbours, so they visit her; she excuses herself from going to them, and is excused.)
One says «امرأةٌ مَقْصورة» and «قَصيرة» and «قَصورة» with one meaning. Kuthayyir ʿAzza said:
4196 - وأنتِ التي حَبَّبْتِ كلَّ قصيرةٍ ... إليَّ ولم تَعْلَمْ بذاك القَصائرُ
عَنَيْتُ قصيراتِ الحِجالِ ولم أُرِدْ ... قِصارَ الخُطا شَرُّ النساءِ البَحاتِرُ (You are the one who made every secluded woman dear to me, though the secluded women do not know it. I meant those kept within the curtained alcoves; I did not mean those short of step — the worst of women are the dumpy ones.)
Al-khiyām is the plural of «خَيْمة», which is made of thumām grass and other herbage; if it is made of hair it is not called khayma but bayt. Jarīr said:
4197 - متى كان الخيامُ بذي طُلوحٍ ... سُقِيْتِ الغَيْثَ أيتها الخيامُ (When were the tents at Dhū Ṭulūḥ? May you be watered with rain, O tents!)

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying: {رَفْرَفٍ}: «الرَّفْرَفُ» is the plural of «رَفْرَفَة», so it is a generic noun (ism jins). It has also been said: rather, it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ); Makkī reported both. It is the fine cloth that hangs down from couches. Al-Jawharī said: "Green cloths from which sitting places are made; the singular is rafrafa." Its derivation is from «رَفَّ الطائرُ», i.e. it rose in the air; and «رَفْرَفَ بجناحَيْه» when it spread them to fly; and the rafraf of clouds is their blowing [along]. Its being a plural is indicated by its being described with a plural. Al-Rāghib said: "The rafīf of trees is the spreading of their branches. «رَفَّ الطائرُ»: it spread its wing, yariffu with kasra. «رَفَّ فَرْخَه يَرُفُّه» with ḍamma: it tended its chick; then it was borrowed for tending. From it: «ماله حافٌّ ولا رافٌّ», i.e. he has no one to surround him and look after him. Al-rafraf is the spread-out [mass] of leaves. And His saying {على رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ}: a kind of cloth likened to meadows. It has also been said: al-rafraf is the edge of the large tent and the pavilion that falls on the ground, short of the ropes and pegs. Al-Ḥasan mentioned that it is cushions." End of quotation. Ibn Jubayr said: "The meadows of Paradise, from «رَفَّ البيتُ» when it is comfortable and fine." From Ibn ʿUyayna: they are carpets. It is described here with «خُضْر» because a generic noun may be described with a plural, as in His saying: {والنخل بَاسِقَاتٍ} [Qāf: 10], and with a singular; its being put in the plural here was made fitting by the plural «حِسان». The majority read «رَفْرَفٍ». ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, ʿĀṣim, al-Jaḥdarī, al-Farqabī and others read «رَفارِفَ خُضْرٍ» in the plural, with a sukūn on the ḍād. From them also «خُضُرٍ» with ḍamma on the ḍād, which is assimilation (itbāʿ) to the khāʾ. It has also been said: it is a dialectal form in the plural of the adjective on the pattern afʿal. A verse of Ṭarafa was cited:
4198 - أيها الفتيانُ في مَجْلِسِنا ... جَرِّدُوا منها وِراداً وشُقُرْ (O young men in our gathering, pick out from them bay horses and chestnuts.)
Another said:
4199 - وما انْتَمَيْتُ إلى خُوْرٍ ولا كُسُف ... ولا لئامٍ غداةَ الرَّوْع أَوْزاعِ (I have never claimed kinship with weaklings, nor with the gloomy-faced, nor with base men scattered on the morning of terror.)
They read «عباقِرِيَّ» with kasra or fatḥa on the qāf and with the yāʾ doubled and with fatḥa, as a diptote. This is problematic, since there is nothing preventing tanwīn on [a word with] the two yāʾs of relation (nisba); it is as if this reader imagined it to be on the pattern mafāʿil and so made it a diptote. Ibn Khālawayh reported from the Prophet ﷺ and a group «وعباقِرِيٍّ» with tanwīn, and «رَفارِفٍ» with full declension is reported from ʿĀṣim. It may be said concerning the one who made «عباقِرِيَّ» a diptote: since it came next to «رفارِفَ», which is a diptote, it was made a diptote for congruence (mushākala); and concerning the one who gave full declension to «رفارِفَ»: since it came next to «عباقريّاً», which is fully declined, he declined it for harmony, as in {سَلاسلاً وأَغْلالاً} [al-Insān: 4], as will come.
Abū Muḥammad al-Marwazī — and he was a grammarian — read «خَضَّارٍ», like «ضَرَّاب», with doubling. [A form] afʿal [paired with] faʿʿāl is not known.
The majority [read] «وعَبْقِرِيٍّ», related to ʿAbqar, which the Arabs claim is the land of the jinn; so everything they considered great and marvelled at they called «عَبْقريٌّ». In the hadith: «فلم أرَ عَبْقَريَّاً يَفْري فَرِيَّه» ("I have not seen a genius doing the work he does"). What is meant by it here, it has been said, is spread carpets with images and figures in them. It has also been said: carpets (al-zarābiyy). It has also been said: rugs (al-ṭanāfis). It has also been said: brocade. And «عَبْقريّ» is the plural of «عَبْقَريَّة», i.e. so it is a generic noun, as was said about «رَفْرف». It has also been said: it is a singular indicating the plural, and for that reason it is described with «حسان».

semin-durr:78-78.t: His saying: {ذِي الجلال}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «ذو الجَلال» with wāw, making it follow the noun [«اسم»]; and thus it is written in the codex of the people of Syria. The rest [read] with yāʾ, as an adjective of «الرَّبِّ», since He is the one described with that. They agreed on the wāw in the first [occurrence], except those I mentioned earlier.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الرحمن}: there are three views on it. One: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "Allah is al-Raḥmān". Two: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is implied, that is: "al-Raḥmān is our Lord". These two views are held by those who regard «الرحمن» together with this implied element as a verse, for they counted «الرحمن» as a verse, and that cannot be conceived except by joining a khabar or a subject to it, since a verse must be informative; this will come at His saying «مُدْهامَّتان». Three: that it is not a verse, and that it forms one utterance with what follows it, being a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «عَلَّم القرآنَ».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {عَلَّمَ القرآن}: there are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is ʿallama taking two objects, that is: "he made known", from taʿlīm (teaching); on this the first object is omitted, and it was said that its implied form is "He taught Jibrīl the Qurʾān"; it was also said "He taught Muḥammad"; it was also said "He taught man", and this is preferable because of its generality, and because His saying «خلق الإِنسانَ» points to it. The second: that it is from ʿalāma (sign), so the meaning is: He made it a sign and a verse to be taken care of.
These clauses were brought without a conjunction because they were put forward to enumerate a favour, as you say: "So-and-so did good to so-and-so: he honoured him, he spread his fame, he raised his rank"; because of the closeness of the connection he left out the conjunction. The apparent sense is that they are reports. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "«خَلَق الإِنسان» is resumptive, and likewise «عَلَّمه» may be an anticipated ḥāl from al-insān, with «قد» intended with it." End of quotation. This is not apparent; rather the apparent sense is what I gave earlier, and al-Zamakhsharī mentioned no other. If it is asked: why did He put the teaching of the Qurʾān to man before his creation when it comes after it in existence? It is said: because teaching is the cause of his being brought into existence and created.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {بِحُسْبَانٍ}: there are three views on it. One: that «الشمس» is a mubtadaʾ and «بحُسْبان» is its khabar, with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being: "the course of the sun and the moon is by a reckoning", that is: existing, or established, or was established, by a reckoning. Two: that the khabar is omitted and this prepositional phrase is attached to it, its implied form being: "they run by a reckoning". On these two views, two views are allowed for al-ḥusbān: one, that it is a single maṣdar, meaning al-ḥisāb, so it is like al-shukrān and al-kufrān; the second, that it is a plural of ḥisāb, like shihāb and shuhbān. Three: that al-ḥusbān is its khabar and the bāʾ is locative, meaning "in", that is: "existing in a ḥusbān"; and ḥusbān on this view is a singular noun, a name for the revolving sphere, likened to the ḥusbān of the mill, by whose revolving the mill turns; Mujāhid said this. [Translator's note: the source repeats «وحُسْبان» three times at this point.]

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {والسمآء رَفَعَهَا}: the majority read with the accusative, by ishtighāl, taking into account the end of the sentence, which the grammarians call "the sentence with two faces" (dhāt al-wajhayn). In it is evidence for Sībawayh, who allows the accusative even if the ishtighāl clause contains no pronoun referring back to the mubtadaʾ contained in the sentence with two faces. Al-Akhfash says: a pronoun is necessary; an example is «هند قامَتْ وعمراً أكرمْتُه لأجلها». He said: "because you took the khabar into account and conjoined to it, and what is conjoined to the khabar is a khabar, so what is required of it is required of this." The majority did not require that, and this is their evidence. Al-Farrāʾ said: "All of them made it accusative without a link, except those among them who were irregular." This was given in full in sūrat Yā Sīn at His saying the Exalted {والقمر قَدَّرْنَاهُ} [Yā Sīn: 39], where the seven differed over its accusative and nominative, and praise be to Allah.
His saying: {وَوَضَعَ الميزان}: the majority read «وَضَع» as a past verb, and «الميزانَ» is accusative as direct object. Ibrāhīm read «ووَضْعَ الميزانِ» with sukūn on the ḍād and genitive «الميزانِ». Its explanation: that it is conjoined to the object of «رَفَعَها», that is: "and He raised the placing of the balance", that is: He gave it standing and elevation for the taking of rights by it; and this is among the wonders of wording, as the implied form becomes: "and He raised the placing of the balance".
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how did He omit the conjunction in the first clauses and bring it afterwards? I say: He rebuked with the first clauses, coming in the manner of enumeration, those who denied al-Raḥmān and His favours, just as one who denies the benefactions of a benefactor is rebuked among people by their being enumerated to him in the example I gave earlier; then He returned the speech to its course after the rebuke, in joining by the conjunction what should be joined, for proportion and nearness. If you ask: what proportion is there between these two clauses that He put the conjunction between them? I say: the sun and moon are heavenly, and the star (al-najm) and the tree are earthly, so there is proportion between them from the aspect of contrast; and the sky and earth are always paired; and the course of the sun and moon by reckoning is of the kind of submission to Allah's command, so it suits the prostration of the star and the tree."

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ}: there are two views about this «أنْ». One: that it is the subjunctive particle, with «لا» after it negative, and «تَطْغَوْا» made accusative by «أنْ», and before it an implied lām of cause, attached to His saying «ووَضَع الميزانَ»; the implied form is: "so that you do not transgress", and this is clear. Al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed that it be the explicative («أنْ» al-mufassira), and on this «لا» is prohibitive and the verb is jussive by it. But the Shaykh rejected it, in that its condition is the preceding of a sentence containing the meaning of saying, and that is not present. I say: Makkī and Abū al-Baqāʾ took the view that it is explicative; but Abū al-Baqāʾ seemed to notice the objection and said: "«وأَنْ» means «أَيْ», and the saying is implied", thereby making the thing explained by «أَنْ» implied, not pronounced. However, it may be said that his statement "the saying is implied" is not good, because it does not explain an explicit saying, so how can he imply what cannot rightly be explained? The remedy is for him to say: "what has the meaning of saying is implied."

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تُخْسِرُواْ}: the majority read with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the sīn, from akhsara, that is: to diminish, as in His saying {وَإِذَا كَالُوهُمْ أَوْ وَّزَنُوهُمْ يُخْسِرُونَ}. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Bilāl ibn Abī Burda read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the sīn, so fa'ala and afʿala are alike in meaning. One says khasira al-mīzān and akhsarahu, with one meaning, like jabara and ajbara. Abū al-Fatḥ and Abū al-Faḍl reported from Bilāl fatḥa on the tāʾ and the sīn. There are two views on it. One: that it is by omission of the preposition, its implied form being: "and do not suffer loss in the balance"; al-Zamakhsharī and Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned it. But the Shaykh said: "There is no need for that, because khasira has come transitively. He the Exalted said: {خسروا أَنْفُسَهُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 12] and {خَسِرَ الدنيا والآخرة} [al-Ḥajj: 11]." I say: This is not of that kind. Do you not see that {خَسِروا أنفسَهم} and {وخَسِر الدنيا والآخرةَ} mean that loss has befallen them, and that they are non-existent? This meaning is certainly not intended in the verse; what is intended is: "do not cause loss to what is weighed in the balance". «تَخْسُروا» was also read, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the sīn. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ولا تَخْسروا» was read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and with ḍamma, kasra and fatḥa on the sīn. One says khasira al-mīzān yakhsiruhu and yakhsuruhu. As for the fatḥa: the original is «في الميزان», so the preposition was dropped and the verb reached it directly." He repeated the word «الميزان» and did not use a pronoun for it in the two clauses after it, to strengthen its importance, and this is like the saying:
4170 - لا أَرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... نَغَّصَ الموتُ ذا الغِنى والفقيرا
(I do not see that anything outstrips death; death has spoiled the life of the rich and the poor.)

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {والأرض وَضَعَهَا}: like His saying {والسمآء رَفَعَهَا} [al-Raḥmān: 7]. Abū al-Sammāl read it nominative, as a mubtadaʾ. And «للأَنام» is the reason for the placing. Al-anām: it was said: living creatures; it was said: the children of Ādam specifically; it was said: they are humankind and jinn. Its pattern is faʿāl like qadhāl, so in the plural of paucity it is ānima, like "āthima woman" (pl.), and in the plural of multiplicity unum, like qadhāl, aqdhila and qudhul.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ}: this clause may be a ḥāl from al-arḍ, but it is an anticipated ḥāl. It is also allowed, and this is the best, that the preposition and its genitive noun be the ḥāl, with «فاكهةٌ» nominative as agent; it is indefinite because benefiting from it is less than benefiting from what is mentioned after it, and this is of the type of ascending from the lower to the higher. Al-akmām: plural of kimm with kasra, which is the vessel of the fruit.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {والحب ذُو العصف والريحان}: Ibn ʿĀmir read all three accusative. There are three views on it. Accusative as ikhtiṣāṣ (specification), that is: "and I specify the grain"; al-Zamakhsharī said this. There is something to consider in it, since it was not included in the meaning of fruit and palm-trees so that He would single it out from among them; he only meant the implying of a verb, which is "I specify", so it is not the technical ikhtiṣāṣ. Two: that it is conjoined to al-arḍ. Makkī said: "because His saying «والأرضَ وَضَعَها» means 'He created it', so He conjoined «الحَبَّ» to that." Three: that it is accusative by an implied «خَلَق», that is: "and He created the grain". Makkī said: "or 'and He created the grain'". And he read thus in agreement with the writing of the codices of his land, for the codices of al-Shām have «ذا» with alif. They allowed for «الرَّيْحان» that it be with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "and possessor of the fragrant herb", so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place, like {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82].
The two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read the first two nominative and «الرَّيْحان» genitive, conjoined to «العَصْفِ», and this supports the statement of the one who omitted the muḍāf in the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir. The rest read all three nominative, conjoined to «فاكهة», that is: "and in it also are these things". He mentioned first what they enjoy of fruits, second the thing that combines enjoyment and nourishment, which is the fruit of the palm, and third what nourishes only, which is the greatest of them, because it is the sustenance of most people. On this reading «الرَّيْحان» may be conjoined to what precedes it, that is: "and in it is also the fragrant herb", or it may be genitive by annexation in origin, that is: "and possessor of the fragrant herb", and what was said earlier is done to it.
Al-ʿaṣf: the leaves of crops. It was said: straw. Its origin, as al-Rāghib said, is from "al-ʿaṣf and al-ʿaṣīfa, which is what is cut (yuʿṣaf) from crops"; it was said: it is the broken bits of plants. The ʿāṣif wind: the one that breaks what it passes over; this has been given. Al-Rayḥān is in origin a maṣdar, then it came to be applied to provision, as in their saying "subḥān Allāh wa-rayḥānuhu", that is: His providing; it was said: al-rayḥān here is the fragrant plant.
There are two statements on al-rayḥān. One: that it is on the pattern faʿlān like al-layyān, from roots with wāw; the original is rawḥān. Abū ʿAlī said: "The wāw was changed to yāʾ, just as they changed yāʾ to wāw in «أَشاوى»." The second: that its origin is rayūḥān, on the pattern fayʿilān, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and the yāʾ assimilated into it, then it was lightened by dropping the middle letter of the word, as they said kaynūna and baynūna. The original has a doubled yāʾ, which was lightened as hayyin and mayyit were lightened. Makkī said: "Lightening it was necessary because of its length, with the addition of the two extra letters." Then he rejected al-Fārisī's statement on the ground that there is no requirement to turn it into yāʾ, and then said: "Some people said", and mentioned what I gave earlier from Abū ʿAlī to the end.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {فَبِأَيِّ}: attached to «تُكذِّبان». The majority add «أيّ» to «الآلاء» by annexation. In the whole sūra «أيّ» was also read with tanwīn, and its explanation is that it cut off ayyan from annexation to an implied thing, then made «آلاء ربِّكما» a badal of it, a badal of a definite from an indefinite. The discussion of «الآلاء» and what its singular is was given in al-Aʿrāf, and praise be to Allah. The address in «رَبِّكما»: it was said to the two weighty ones, humans and jinn, because al-anām includes both according to the well-known view; it was said: to male and female; it was said: it is a dual that is meant for one, as in His saying the Exalted {أَلْقِيَا فِي جَهَنَّمَ} [Qāf: 24] and the saying of al-Khabīth al-Thaqafī, «يا حَرَسيُّ اضْربا عُنُقَه» ("O guard, strike (dual) his neck"); what is in it has been given. And «كالفَخَّار» is an adjective of ṣalṣāl, and its explanation was given.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
And al-jānn: it was said: it is a generic noun like al-insān. It was said: it is the father of the jinn, Iblīs. It was said: it is their father but not Iblīs.
His saying: {مِن مَّارِجٍ مِّن نَّارٍ}: the first «مِن» is for the beginning of the limit. As for the second there are two views: one, that it is explicative; the second, that it is partitive. Al-mārij: it was said: what is mixed of red, yellow and green, and this is observable in fire, where the three colours are seen mixed with one another. It was said: the pure. It was said: the red. It was said: the redness at the edge of the fire. It was said: what is mixed with black. It was said: the pure. It was said: the flickering flame. And «مِنْ نار» is an adjective of «مارج». His saying «فبأيِّ» to the end is emphasis and repetition, as was given in His saying {وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا القرآن} [al-Qamar: 21] and as in what will come: {وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ} [al-Mursalāt: 15]. A group, among them Ibn Qutayba, held that the repetition is because of the variety of favours, so He repeated the challenge with each single one.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {رَبُّ المشرقين}: the majority read it nominative. There are two views on it. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «مَرَج البحرَيْن», and what is between them is parenthetical. The second: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "He is the Lord", meaning the one who did these things. The third: that it is a badal of the pronoun in «خَلَق». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «ربِّ» genitive, as a badal or bayān of «ربِّكما». Makkī said: "In speech the genitive is allowed as a badal of «ربِّكما»", as if he had not learned that it is a transmitted reading. As for al-mashriqān, it was said: the east of winter and summer and their two wests. It was said: the two easts of the sun and moon and their two wests. It was said: the two easts of the sun only and its two wests. The Shaykh said: "From ʿAbbās: the sun has an east in summer that is ascending, and an east in winter that is descending; it moves between them ascending and descending." The Shaykh said: "So al-mashriqān and al-maghribān are for the sun." I say: This is the statement that says: the east of summer and the east of winter, for by them he means only the sun's and the moon's rising in them, or the sun's rising alone in them, so it falls necessarily within one of the two statements mentioned.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {يَلْتَقِيَانِ}: a ḥāl from «البحرَيْنِ», and it is close to the anticipated ḥāl. It may, with some stretching, be concurrent. And «بينهما بَرْزَخٌ» may be a resumptive clause, or a ḥāl, or the adverbial alone may be the ḥāl, with al-barzakh as agent of it, and this is best because of its nearness to a single word. As for the owner of the ḥāl there are two views: one, that it is «البحرَيْن»; the second, that it is the agent of «يَلْتقيان». And «لا يَبْغِيان» is another ḥāl like the one before it, that is: "He let them flow, not transgressing", or "they meet, not transgressing", or "between them is a barrier in the state of their not transgressing". This ḥāl is in the force of a reason, since the meaning is: "so that they do not transgress". Some have strained and said: the original of that is "so that they do not transgress", then the particle of reason was dropped, which is regular with «أَنْ» and «أَنَّ», then «أَنْ» was also dropped, which is a regular omission, as in His saying the Exalted {وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ يُرِيكُمُ} [al-Rūm: 24]; so when «أَنْ» was dropped, the verb became nominative. This is not prohibited, except that omission is repeated in it, and he may say: omission has come more than that in what is more hidden than this, as was given in {قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ} [al-Najm: 9], and as will come in His saying {وَتَجْعَلُونَ رِزْقَكُمْ} [al-Wāqiʿa: 82].

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {يَخْرُجُ}: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read «يُخْرَج», passive. The rest read active, figuratively. They said: there is an omitted muḍāf, that is: "from one of them", because that is not taken from the sweet sea, so that they faulted the saying:
4171 - فجاءَ بها ما شِئتَ مِنْ لَطَمِيَّةٍ ... على وَجْهِها ماءُ الفُراتِ يموجُ
(And he brought it, as much as you wish of musk-laden wares, on whose surface the water of the Euphrates surges.)
Makkī said: "as He the Exalted said: {على رَجُلٍ مِّنَ القريتين} [al-Zukhruf: 31], that is: from one of the two towns, and the omission of the muḍāf is frequent and common." It was said: it is like His saying {نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا} [al-Kahf: 61], whereas the one who forgot was his servant (Mūsā's young companion); this is attributed to Abū ʿUbayda. It was said: from one of them comes the pearl, and from the other the coral. It was said: rather, both come out from both, and then they mentioned interpretations, among them: that the two come out of the salt sea at the place where the sweet falls into it, and this is observed by divers and is the view of the majority, so attributing it to both is fitting. Among them is the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās: these things come to be in the sea by the falling of rain, and the oysters open their mouths to the rain, and people have witnessed it. Among them: that the sweet in the salt is like fertilization, as it is said that the child comes out from the male and the female. Among them: that it was said «منهما» in that they are one kind, so the coming out of these things is from both, as the Exalted said {وَجَعَلَ القمر فِيهِنَّ نُوراً} [Nūḥ: 16], though it is in only one of them.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why did He say «منهما» when they come out only from the salt? I say: when the two met and became like one thing, it was allowed to say they come out from both, as it is said 'they come out of the sea' and they do not come out of the whole sea, but from part of it. You say 'I went out of the town', though you went out only from a quarter of its quarters, from one house of its houses. It was also said: they come out only from the meeting-place of the salt and the sweet." End of quotation. Some said: the speech of Allah is more deserving of consideration than the speech of some people, so it is possible that He drives them from the sweet sea to the salt, and it happened that they extracted them only from the salt; and if on land there are things hidden from merchants who go back and forth crossing deserts, how much more what is in the depth of the sea? The answer to this: Allah the Exalted addresses people and reminds them of His favour only with what they are familiar with and witness.
Al-luʾluʾ: it was said: the large gems; and al-marjān its small ones; it was also said the reverse, and they quoted al-Aʿshā's saying:
4172 - مِنْ كلِّ مَرْجانةٍ في البحرِ أَحْرَزها ... تَيَّارُها ووقاها طِيْنَها الصَّدَفُ
(Of every pearl in the sea, which its current secured and whose mud the oyster guarded.)
He meant the large pearl. It was said: al-marjān is a red stone. It was said: a very white stone. Al-marjān is non-Arabic. Ibn Durayd said: "I have not heard a conjugated verb from it. And al-luʾluʾ is a rare pattern; only five words have come on this form: al-luʾluʾ, al-juʾjuʾ, which is the chest, al-duʾduʾ, al-yuʾyuʾ for a bird, and al-buʾbuʾ with two bāʾs, which is the original. Al-luʾluʾ with two ḍammas and hamza is the well-known form, and changing the hamza into wāw is common and eloquent, and this was given earlier."
Ṭalḥa read «اللُّؤْلِىءُ» with kasra on the third lām, and it is a preserved dialect. Abū al-Faḍl reported from him «اللُّؤْلِيْ» with the last hamza changed into a yāʾ with sukūn, as if, when he put kasra on what precedes the hamza, he changed it into yāʾ out of heaviness. Abū ʿAmr in one transmission read «يُخْرِجُ», that is, Allah the Exalted. It is also reported from him and from Ibn Miqsam «نُخْرِجُ» with the nūn of majesty. Al-luʾluʾ and al-marjān are accusative in these two readings.
